title: Quality-unit oversight, with citations
근거로 확인하는 품질부서 감독
description: Three company-specific observations and questions for reviewing your own records.
회사별 관찰사항 3가지와 내부 기록 검토를 위한 질문입니다.
input: Using the saved FDA Drug warning letters, give three specific examples of quality-unit oversight deficiencies. Attribute each observation to its company and cite the source. End with two conditional questions a quality team could use to review its own records, and state the limits of this comparison.

sections.title: Answer
sections.text:
1) Dabur India Limited — Quality-unit oversight did not prevent record falsification and data/reporting discrepancies: an investigator found a newly produced logbook that was falsified (omitting U.S. marketed OTC products) and identified multiple discrepancies between source analytical data and final reported values in batch records/CoAs [1].

2) Reliance Life Sciences Private Limited — Quality-unit oversight failed to ensure integrity and completeness of laboratory/microbiological records: management interviews and inspection evidence indicated microbiological samples were never collected and recordkeeping was inaccurate, raising questions about data authenticity and product quality; the firm’s remediation plan lacked sufficient detail and timelines [3].

3) Apotex Inc. — Quality unit oversight of aseptic processing was insufficient in frequency and depth: the FDA noted deficiencies in production management oversight and explicitly cited the need for appropriate frequency and depth of quality unit oversight (e.g., audits, ad hoc and daily interactions) of aseptic processing and support operations [2].

Two conditional review questions a quality team could use on its own records:
- If you perform a retrospective review, do your logbooks, analytical data books, and batch records consistently match with no unexplained omissions or alterations?
- If you assess aseptic processing, do documented quality-unit activities (audits, routine interactions, investigations) show sufficient frequency, depth, and follow-through to detect and correct contamination/control issues?

Limits of this comparison: these examples are drawn only from the provided FDA warning-letter excerpts and do not represent the full inspection reports, the firms’ complete responses, or an overall assessment of any firm’s compliance.

title: Contamination controls across companies
회사별 오염관리 관찰사항 비교
description: A research brief with findings, evidence checks and unanswered applicability questions.
발견사항, 근거 점검, 추가 확인 질문을 담은 리서치 보고서입니다.
input: Compare contamination-control observations in at least two companies' saved FDA Drug warning letters. Identify three to five source-supported findings, explain what differs between the cases, and provide conditional review questions for a team that manufactures sterile products. Clearly separate observed source facts from unanswered applicability questions. This is a public demonstration draft, not a compliance decision.

sections.title: Comparative summary of contamination-control observations from FDA warning letters (public demonstration draft)
items:
Wizcure Pharmaa: FDA observed lack of physical barrier separating the ISO 5 (Grade A) filling zone from the surrounding ISO 7 (Grade B), equipment parts in direct contact with drug product were not sterilized, inadequate space and equipment in poor repair, and lack of a meaningful environmental and personnel monitoring program for the aseptic line. [S2]
Finding is limited to FDA's observations in the Wizcure Pharmaa warning letter; the company’s corrective actions described in its response are not independently verified here.

Global Pharma Healthcare: FDA found the environmental monitoring (EM) program inadequate, including no non-viable air samples inside the Grade A filling zone or Grade B surrounding areas during active filling, no studies demonstrating disinfectant would not interfere with swabs for viable surface monitoring, and lack of identification data on isolates recovered from EM and personnel monitoring. [S3]
Finding reflects FDA’s documented observations at Global Pharma and the agency’s critique of the company's response timing; it does not assess the firm's current EM program.

International Medication Systems: FDA documented severe environmental contamination (including insect larvae and gross microbial contamination) in the aseptic processing area; FDA found the firm’s root-cause explanation (insect infiltration of sealed plates) unsupported and criticized the decision to release product manufactured under those conditions. [S1]
Finding is taken from FDA’s description of the inspection and the firm’s investigation; it does not evaluate the firm’s subsequent actions or current state.

Differences between cases: Wizcure’s deficiencies emphasize facility design/separation, equipment sterilization, space and maintenance, and monitoring gaps (S2); Global Pharma’s deficiencies center on EM program design, sampling timing, and laboratory identification/data (S3); International Medication Systems documents acute visible contamination events and a deficient investigation/product release decision (S1). [S2, S3, S1]
Comparison synthesizes separate FDA observations; it does not imply these firms share root causes or that one firm’s controls map to another’s.

sections.title: Review questions
items: If our sterile product lines use ISO-classified zones, do we have physical barriers or RABS protecting ISO 5 zones from adjacent ISO 7 traffic, and are there documented validation studies showing barrier efficacy?

Are environmental monitoring locations and timing defined to sample inside Grade A (ISO 5) and surrounding Grade B (ISO 7) during active filling, including non-viable air sampling and personnel monitoring?
Do our EM procedures include validated methods to demonstrate disinfectant neutralization or lack of interference with viable surface/swab recovery and identification and trending of isolates?
Do we have documented procedures and records showing equipment and direct-contact parts are sterilized or otherwise demonstrated suitable before contact with sterile product?

If an acute contamination event (e.g., visible gross contamination or insect evidence) occurs, do our investigation and product disposition procedures require scientifically-supported root-cause analysis and prevent product release pending adequate justification?

sources.label: International Medication Systems Limited
sources.excerpt:
Your investigation failed to identify a scientifically-supported root cause, instead attributing these exceedingly high environmental monitoring findings to an unsubstantiated hypothesis involving insect infiltration of sealed monitoring plates. Notably, written procedures require inspection of plates before use to ensure they are not contaminated or defective, and also require very strict handling measures following sampling (e.g., (b)(4) bags, sterile tape). The microbiological growth media batch also passed negative control testing. Although your deviation report lacked evidence of defects or sampling error, you assessed the contamination risk as “low” based on overreliance on passing sterility test results, and the quality unit approved the release of epinephrine injection, lot EA038A5.
The presence of insect larvae and gross microbial contamination in your aseptic processing area demonstrates a critical failure of your contamination control program. The decision to release a lot manufactured under these conditions also demonstrates that your quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products are manufactured under appropriate conditions and to reject any lot produced under conditions that compromise its quality.
In your response, you reiterate that your investigation concluded the contamination was “post-exposure adventitious contamination external to the filling suite,” based on mostly acceptable environmental monitoring data in other locations that day. Using this rationale, you determined the two environmental contamination events were isolated incidents and the risk to the product was low. You also determined that no corrective actions were needed.
Your response is inadequate. Your investigation outcome based on a “post-exposure” hypothesis remains poorly supported by data. The occurrence of two severe contamination events on the same day in adjacent rooms indicates a significant breakdown in contamination control. Additionally, your failure to implement corrective actions reflects a critical deficiency in your investigation and indicates inadequate oversight of the state of control of the aseptic processing operation.

sources.label: Wizcure Pharmaa Private Limited
sources.excerpt:
2. Your firm failed to perform operations within specifically defined areas of adequate size and to have separate or defined areas or such other control systems necessary to prevent contamination or mix-ups in aseptic processing areas (21 CFR 211.42(c)(10).
Your aseptic manufacturing filling line used to produce over-the-counter (OTC) sterile drug products is inadequate.
For example, the inspection documented that your filling line has no physical barrier separating and protecting your ISO 5 (Grade A) aseptic filling line from the surrounding ISO 7 (Grade B) room and its personnel. The absence of a physical barrier separating the ISO 5 (Grade A) filling zone from the ISO 7 (Grade B) surrounding environment creates an unacceptable risk to product sterility.
Furthermore, several equipment parts in direct contact with drug product, containers, and closures were not sterilized.
It is essential that the ISO 5 (Grade A) environment continuously maintains an extremely high level of air cleanliness to protect the exposed sterile drug product from contamination. Without proper physical separation, the integrity of the aseptic processing environment cannot be reliably maintained as air currents, personnel movement, and other variables in the less-controlled ISO 7 space can directly convey contamination into the ISO 5 zone.
In addition, to ensure sterility, it is imperative that only sterile equipment comes into direct contact with the sterile formulation, containers, and closures.
Your aseptic processing room also had inadequate space to accommodate appropriate ergonomics, personnel flow, and material flow. Our inspection also found that your processing equipment was in poor state of repair, as detailed later in this letter.
Finally, you lacked a meaningful environmental monitoring (e.g., critical surfaces, viable air) and personnel monitoring program for your aseptic processing line.
Aseptic manufacturing processes operations must be performed in specifically defined areas of adequate size and vigilantly monitored to promptly identify microbial hazards before there is a non-sterility consequence.
In your response, you commit to replacing your (b)(4) filling line with a restricted access barrier system (RABS) and implementing a comprehensive environmental monitoring program.

sources.label: Global Pharma Healthcare Private Limited
sources.excerpt:
Your environmental monitoring (EM) program (including personnel monitoring (PM)) was inadequate for classified areas used to produce sterile ophthalmic drug products. For example, non-viable air samples were not collected inside the Grade A filling zone or the Grade B surrounding areas during active filling, you lacked studies to demonstrate that residual disinfectant would not interfere with the swabs used for viable surface monitoring, and you lacked identification data on isolates recovered from EM and PM sampling. Vigilant and responsive environmental and personnel monitoring programs should be designed to provide meaningful information on the state of control of your aseptic processing environment. Operations that include highly manually intensive aseptic activities warrant a more extensive environmental and personnel monitoring program, including but not limited to, heightened emphasis on well-timed sampling to appropriately monitor batch manufacturing conditions.
In your response, you mention a limited number of environmental samples taken in January 2023 were sent to a third-party laboratory and these samples did not reveal Pseudomonas aeruginosa in your environment. This response is inadequate. The last batches of Artificial Tears shipped to the United States had been manufactured many months before (in April 2022) your limited sampling was conducted, according to records provided by your firm. Environmental sampling that occurs several months after batch manufacture is of little temporal significance. There is also minimal scientific value in testing sterile drug manufacturing areas solely for the presence of a single microbial species. You also had batch retain samples tested by a third-party laboratory and you reported in your response that these samples did not fail sterility testing. However, it is not unexpected that sterility testing of retains of otherwise contaminated batches may pass sterility testing because of the non-uniform nature of microbiological contamination. As noted above, many of your firm’s batches were found to be non-sterile upon FDA testing and were associated with grave adverse events.
In response to this letter, provide the following:
• A comprehensive, independent assessment of the design and control of your firm’s manufacturing operations, with a detailed and thorough review of all microbiological hazards.

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: FDA inspected Dabur India Limited (FEI 3001413302) from January 12–16, 2026 and identified significant violations of CGMP (21 CFR parts 210 and 211). FDA concluded the firm’s methods, facilities, or controls do not conform to CGMP and that the firm’s drug products are adulterated under section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B)). Key observations included: a deficient Quality Unit that signed off on records with apparent falsification and transcription discrepancies; incomplete laboratory records and missing microbiological plates; inadequate cleaning and cleaning validation for non-dedicated equipment; and lack of process validation for many marketed OTC products. FDA recommended a qualified CGMP consultant, requested extensive remedial submissions for each deficiency, noted a voluntary recall for some products, and placed all drugs offered for import from the firm on Import Alert 66-40 on June 5, 2026.

sections.title: Quality Unit oversight and record review authority
sections.text: FDA observed the Quality Unit (QU) signed off on records that included a falsified equipment logbook and analytical data discrepancies; FDA states the QU failed to ensure data integrity and completeness (e.g., discovery of a falsified logbook and discrepancies between source analytical data and final batch records). Review whether your QU has explicit authority, documented procedures, and resourcing to identify and escalate suspected record falsification, transcription errors, and to perform complete final batch reviews before disposition decisions.

sections.title: Laboratory data completeness and sample traceability
sections.text: FDA found laboratory notebooks and records lacking complete data (missing microbiology plates, absence of test procedures and analytical workbooks for multiple batches, and missing equipment logbook entries). Examine controls for sample handling, retention and disposal, lab record completeness (analytical notebooks, workbooks, test data sheets), and instrument usage logs to ensure all test results are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, and accurate.

sections.title: Cleaning validation and controls for non-dedicated equipment
sections.text: FDA identified reliance on visual inspection only, absence of established carryover limits, lack of quantitative residue testing and no cleaning validation for some multi-product lines. Review cleaning validation programs, worst-case identification, swab/surface sampling plans, and interim controls for cross-contamination when equipment is non-dedicated.

sections.title: Process validation plans and interim controls
sections.text: FDA observed that process validation had not been performed for many marketed products and that the firm did not provide timeframes or interim controls (e.g., enhanced finished-product testing) for products produced before validation. Verify that process validation strategies include timelines, product-specific plans, and interim risk-mitigation measures for products already manufactured and distributed.

sections.title: Distribution, recall readiness, and Import Alert implications
sections.text: FDA recommended removal of certain batches, the firm initiated a voluntary recall for some products, and FDA placed the firm on Import Alert 66-40. Review procedures for customer notification, recall execution, product disposition, and regulatory reporting in the event of import refusals or broader market actions.

Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality control unit with the responsibility and authority to approve or reject all components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, packaging materials, labeling, and drug products and the authority to review production records to assure that no errors have occurred or, if errors have occurred, that they have been fully investigated (21 CFR 211.22(a)).
sources.excerpt:
1. Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality control unit with the responsibility and authority to approve or reject all components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, packaging materials, labeling, and drug products and the authority to review production records to assure that no errors have occurred or, if errors have occurred, that they have been fully investigated (21 CFR 211.22(a)).
Your firm manufactures over-the-counter drug products including (b)(4) and (b)(4) . Your quality unit (QU) failed to exercise its authority and responsibilities over your drug manufacturing operations, including ensuring the integrity of your production records.
During the inspection, our investigator requested the equipment usage logbook for Unit (b)(4) , Line (b)(4) , which your management stated was dedicated exclusively to (b)(4) manufacturing. Your firm delayed providing this record for several days. When your firm finally produced the logbook, it appeared to have been newly created. Subsequently, our investigator discovered the original logbook in the document room. A comparison of the two logbooks revealed that the version provided to our investigator was falsified. The fraudulent logbook listed entries only for (b)(4) . It deliberately omitted multiple U.S. marketed OTC drug products that were documented in the original logbook, including (b)(4) .
Furthermore, our investigator identified multiple discrepancies between the source data in your analytical data books and the final values reported in your batch manufacturing records or certificates of analysis. For multiple batches of (b)(4) and (b)(4) , the reported values for quality attributes such as residue on ignition, melting range, pH, and viscosity did not match the original data. While these inaccuracies did not involve out-of-specification results, your QU signed off on these records without ensuring the consistency and accuracy of the data.
In your response, you acknowledge these deficiencies, attributing the falsified logbook to “inadequate documentation controls, insufficient oversight, and lack of robust governance.” You attributed other data inaccuracies to your transcription practices and inadequate resources within your QU for proper review. You state that you trained personnel on data integrity and committed to revising procedures and reviewing only the (b)(4) of data for similar transcription errors. You also commit to sending “ (b)(4) samples of impacted drug product including (b)(4) ” to a contract testing laboratory.
Your response is inadequate because it fails to address the severity of the observed data integrity failures. Your proposed corrective actions address the data integrity breaches as isolated procedural gaps rather than as evidence of a systemic breakdown in QU oversight and a deficient quality culture. Your response does not address the fundamental failure of your QU to ensure the integrity and completeness of all data related to your drug manufacturing operations, nor does it include an adequate assessment of the potential impact on the quality of drug products already distributed to the U.S. market. Furthermore, your response lacks a sufficient comprehensive evaluation of your QU’s capabilities to fulfill all required quality-related functions.
Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. See FDA’s guidance document Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical CGMP Regulations for help implementing quality systems and risk management approaches to meet the requirements of CGMP regulations 21 CFR, parts 210 and 211 at https://www.fda.gov/media/71023/download.
In response to this letter, provide:
A comprehensive assessment of documentation systems used throughout your manufacturing and laboratory operations to determine where documentation practices are insufficient. Include a detailed corrective action and preventive action (CAPA) plan that comprehensively remediates your firm’s documentation practices to ensure you retain attributable, legible, complete, original, accurate, contemporaneous records throughout your operation.
A comprehensive assessment and remediation plan to ensure your QU is given the authority and resources to effectively function. The assessment should also include, but not be limited to: o A determination of whether procedures used by your firm are robust and appropriate o Provisions for QU oversight throughout your operations to evaluate adherence to appropriate practices o A complete and final review of each batch and its related information before the QU disposition decision o Oversight and approval of investigations and discharging of all other QU duties to ensure identity, strength, quality, and purity of all products.

sources.label: Dabur India Limited · 2. Your firm failed to ensure that laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests necessary to ensure compliance with established specifications and standards (21 CFR 211.194(a)).
sources.excerpt:
2. Your firm failed to ensure that laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests necessary to ensure compliance with established specifications and standards (21 CFR 211.194(a)).
Your laboratory records did not include complete data to support the analyses performed. For example, your analytical notebooks documented approximately (b)(4) microbiology plates for finished drug products and approximately (b)(4) media plates for testing (b)(4) samples as incubated, but the plates were physically absent from incubators with no documented explanation about their whereabouts or disposal. In addition, during the inspection you could not produce the test procedures, analytical workbooks, or test data sheets to support the reported certificate of analysis results for approximately (b)(4) batches of U.S. marketed drug products. You also failed to make the required entries in your equipment logbooks to reflect the use of multiple instruments for the specific batch release tests performed.
In your response, you indicate that a microbiologist inadvertently discarded the missing microbiological plates due to lack of training. You state that you retrained the microbiologist, re-analyzed the missing finished drug product plates, and introduced a new controlled logbook to improve sample traceability.
Regarding the batches released without supporting analytical records, you commit to sending samples for several of the batches to a contract laboratory for retrospective testing and to implementing formal test data sheets for future data recording. Further, you state that you have retrained the personnel responsible for failing to document instrument usage and that you will discontinue the use of separate equipment usage logbooks once the new data sheets are implemented.
Your response is inadequate because it does not adequately address major deficiencies in your laboratory system. Your response does not address your oversight of data integrity including, but not limited to, improving your quality assurance function. Your response does not provide a comprehensive retrospective risk assessment or complete testing of all potentially impacted drug products within expiry and fails to adequately assess and mitigate the risk to consumers.
Reliability of data is fundamentally compromised when there is a failure to record data or to maintain complete and accurate records of test results. Furthermore, the lack of reliable data compromises the ability of your QU to exercise its function of ensuring compliance to applicable standards.
Your quality system does not adequately ensure the accuracy and integrity of data to support the safety, effectiveness, and quality of the drugs you manufacture. See FDA’s guidance document Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Questions and Answers for guidance on establishing and following CGMP compliant data integrity practices at https://www.fda.gov/media/119267/download.
We strongly recommend that you retain an independent third-party qualified consultant to assist in your remediation. In response to this letter, provide:
A comprehensive investigation into the extent of the inaccuracies in data records and reporting. Your investigation should include: o A detailed investigation protocol and methodology; a summary of all laboratories, manufacturing operations, and systems to be covered by the assessment; and a justification for any part of your operation that you propose to exclude. o Interviews of current and former employees to identify the nature, scope, and root cause of data inaccuracies. We recommend that these interviews be conducted by a qualified third party. o An assessment of the extent of data integrity deficiencies at your facility. Identify omissions, alterations, deletions, record destruction, non-contemporaneous record completion, and other deficiencies. Describe all parts of your facility’s operations in which you discovered data integrity lapses. o A comprehensive retrospective evaluation of the nature of all data integrity deficiencies. We recommend that a qualified third party with specific expertise in the area where potential breaches were identified should evaluate all data integrity lapses.
A current risk assessment of the potential effects of the observed failures on the quality of your drugs. Your assessment should include analyses of the risks to patients caused by the release of drugs affected by a lapse of data integrity and analyses of the risks posed by ongoing operations.
A management strategy for your firm that includes the details of your global corrective action and preventive action plan. Your strategy should include: o A detailed corrective action plan that describes how you intend to ensure the reliability and completeness of all the data you generate including analytical data, manufacturing records, and all data submitted to FDA. o A comprehensive description of the root causes of your data integrity lapses including evidence that the scope and depth of the current action plan is commensurate with the findings of the investigation and risk assessment. Indicate whether individuals responsible for data integrity lapses remain able to influence CGMP-related or drug application data at your firm. o Interim measures describing the actions you have taken or will take to protect patients and to ensure the quality of your drugs, such as notifying your customers, recalling product, conducting additional testing, adding lots to your stability programs to assure stability, drug application actions, and enhanced complaint monitoring. o Long-term measures describing any remediation efforts and enhancements to procedures, processes, methods, controls, systems, management oversight, and human resources (e.g., training, staffing improvements) designed to ensure the integrity of your company’s data. o A commitment to have a qualified consultant conduct extensive annual audits, for at least two years, to assist in evaluating CAPA effectiveness after you have executed your data integrity remediation protocol. o Inform FDA if you will be hiring a Chief Integrity Officer who is fully empowered to receive anonymous complaints from employees reporting data integrity concerns and with the authority to ensure any potential breach is promptly investigated (by independent quality assurance function, along with expertise from outside entities whenever needed). o A status report for any of the above activities already underway or completed.

sources.label: Dabur India Limited · 3. Your firm failed to establish and follow adequate written procedures for cleaning and maintenance of equipment (21 CFR 211.67(b)).
sources.excerpt:
3. Your firm failed to establish and follow adequate written procedures for cleaning and maintenance of equipment (21 CFR 211.67(b)).
You failed to demonstrate that your cleaning practices are adequate to remove potential contaminants and to prevent drug product carry over in shared equipment used to manufacture your OTC drug products.
For example, your cleaning validation program for the non-dedicated Unit (b)(4) Line (b)(4) relied exclusively on the visual inspection of (b)(4) to determine adequate cleaning. Your cleaning validation program lacked scientifically determined maximum allowable carryover limits, quantitative residue testing, or direct surface sampling of difficult-to-clean areas. In addition, you did not perform any cleaning validation for Unit (b)(4) Line (b)(4) despite using it to manufacture at least (b)(4) different OTC drug products.
In your response, you acknowledge the deficiencies in your cleaning validation program. You commit to enhancing your cleaning validation program by developing validated analytical methods, establishing carryover limits, implementing direct surface swab sampling, and revalidating the cleaning process. You stated that Line (b)(4) is now dedicated to a (b)(4) drug product, and you are conducting a limited retrospective quality review by testing only (b)(4) samples for potential cross-contamination.
Your response is inadequate because it does not address the interim controls you will implement to mitigate the risk of cross-contamination during your remediation period. Additionally, testing only (b)(4) samples from the (b)(4) batches manufactured on Line (b)(4) is statistically insufficient to assess the potential for cross-contamination. Further, your response also does not include a retrospective review of all drug products released to the U.S. market and within expiry for potential cross-contamination resulting from the use of a non-validated cleaning process on non-dedicated equipment.
Inadequate removal of active ingredients and drug product residues from surfaces of non-dedicated manufacturing equipment can lead to contamination of drug products subsequently manufactured on that equipment.
In response to this letter, provide:
Your CAPA plan to implement routine, vigilant operations management oversight of facilities and equipment. This plan should incorporate oversight from a qualified independent consultant and ensure, among other things, prompt detection of equipment/facilities performance issues, effective execution of repairs, adherence to appropriate preventive maintenance schedules, timely technological upgrades to the equipment/facility infrastructure, and improved systems for ongoing management review. Your plan should also ensure that appropriate actions are taken throughout the company network.
A comprehensive, independent retrospective assessment of your cleaning effectiveness to evaluate the scope of cross-contamination hazards. Include the identity of residues, other manufacturing equipment that may have been improperly cleaned, and an assessment whether cross-contaminated drug products may have been released for distribution. The assessment should identify any inadequacies of cleaning procedures and practices, and encompass each piece of manufacturing equipment used to manufacture more than one drug product.
Appropriate improvements to your cleaning validation program, with special emphasis on incorporating conditions identified as worst case in your drug manufacturing operation. This should include but not be limited to identification and evaluation of all worst-case: o drugs with higher toxicities o drugs with higher drug potencies o drugs of lower solubility in their cleaning solvents o drugs with characteristics that make them difficult to clean o swabbing locations for areas that are most difficult to clean o maximum hold times before cleaning
In addition, describe the steps that must be taken in your change management system before introduction of new manufacturing equipment or a new drug product.
A summary of updated SOPs that ensure an appropriate program is in place for verification and validation of cleaning procedures for drug products, processes, and equipment.

Your firm failed to establish adequate written procedures for production and process control designed to assure that the drug products you manufacture have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess, and your firm’s quality control unit did not review and approve those procedures, including any changes (21 CFR 211.100(a)).

4. Your firm failed to establish adequate written procedures for production and process control designed to assure that the drug products you manufacture have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess, and your firm’s quality control unit did not review and approve those procedures, including any changes (21 CFR 211.100(a)).
You failed to validate your manufacturing process for your OTC drug products. During the inspection, you stated that you had not performed process validation for (b)(4) of the (b)(4) drug products you manufacture on Unit (b)(4) lines. You also stated you had not performed process validation for (b)(4) of the (b)(4) drug products you manufacture on Unit (b)(4) lines.
In your response, you acknowledge the lack of process validation for most of your drug products and commit to preparing process validation plans and protocols using a campaign-based approach.
Your response is inadequate because it does not provide a schedule or timeframes for completing process validation activities for each of your drug products. Furthermore, your response lacks an interim plan, such as enhanced finished drug product testing, for any drugs manufactured and distributed before these validation activities are completed to ensure you produce drug products of acceptable quality. You also did not provide drug product impact assessments for U.S. distributed drug products within expiry and ongoing manufacturing.
Process validation evaluates the soundness of design and state of control of a process throughout its lifecycle. Each significant stage of a manufacturing process must be designed appropriately and assure the quality of raw material inputs, in-process materials, and finished drugs. Process qualification studies include intensive monitoring and testing throughout each significant process stage to characterize intra-batch variation and evaluate batches to determine whether an initial state of control has been established.
Successful process qualification studies are necessary before commercial distribution. Thereafter, ongoing vigilant oversight of process performance and drug product quality is necessary to ensure you maintain a stable manufacturing operation throughout the drug product lifecycle. See FDA’s guidance for industry, Process Validation: General Principles and Practices , for general principles and approaches that the FDA considers appropriate elements of process validation at https://www.fda.gov/media/71021/download.
In response to this letter, provide:
A detailed summary of your validation program for ensuring a state of control throughout the product lifecycle, along with associated procedures. Describe your program for process performance qualification and ongoing monitoring of both intra-batch and inter-batch variation to ensure a continuing state of control.
A timeline for performing process performance qualification for each of your marketed drug products.
Process performance protocols, and written procedures for qualification of equipment and facilities.
A detailed program for designing, validating, maintaining, controlling, and monitoring each of your manufacturing processes that includes vigilant monitoring of intra-batch and inter-batch variation to ensure an ongoing state of control. Also, include your program for qualification of your equipment and facility.

Conclusion
The violations cited in this letter are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of violations that exist at your facility. You are responsible for investigating and determining the causes of any violations and for preventing their recurrence or the occurrence of other violations.
FDA placed all drugs and drug products offered for import into the United States from your firm on Import Alert 66-40 on June 5, 2026.
Correct any violations promptly. FDA may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer until any violations are completely addressed and we confirm your compliance with CGMP. We may re-inspect to verify that you have completed corrective actions to any violations.
Failure to address any violations may also result in the FDA continuing to refuse admission of articles manufactured at Dabur India Limited, at Survey No. 225/4/1, Village: Saily, Silvassa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, into the United States under section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 381(a)(3). This letter notifies you of our findings and provides you an opportunity to address the above deficiencies. After you receive this letter, respond to this office in writing within 15 working days. Specify what you have done to address any violations and to prevent their recurrence. In response to this letter, you may provide additional information for our consideration as we continue to assess your activities and practices. If you cannot complete corrective actions within 15 working days, state your reasons for delay and your schedule for completion.
Send your electronic reply to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov. Identify your response with FEI 3001413302 and ATTN: Rokhsana Safaai-Jazi.

Your firm manufactures over-the-counter drug products including (b)(4) and (b)(4) . Your quality unit (QU) failed to exercise its authority and responsibilities over your drug manufacturing operations, including ensuring the integrity of your production records.
During the inspection, our investigator requested the equipment usage logbook for Unit (b)(4) , Line (b)(4) , which your management stated was dedicated exclusively to (b)(4) manufacturing. Your firm delayed providing this record for several days. When your firm finally produced the logbook, it appeared to have been newly created. Subsequently, our investigator discovered the original logbook in the document room. A comparison of the two logbooks revealed that the version provided to our investigator was falsified. The fraudulent logbook listed entries only for (b)(4) . It deliberately omitted multiple U.S. marketed OTC drug products that were documented in the original logbook, including (b)(4) .
Furthermore, our investigator identified multiple discrepancies between the source data in your analytical data books and the final values reported in your batch manufacturing records or certificates of analysis. For multiple batches of (b)(4) and (b)(4) , the reported values for quality attributes such as residue on ignition, melting range, pH, and viscosity did not match the original data. While these inaccuracies did not involve out-of-specification results, your QU signed off on these records without ensuring the consistency and accuracy of the data.
In your response, you acknowledge these deficiencies, attributing the falsified logbook to “inadequate documentation controls, insufficient oversight, and lack of robust governance.” You attributed other data inaccuracies to your transcription practices and inadequate resources within your QU for proper review. You state that you trained personnel on data integrity and committed to revising procedures and reviewing only the (b)(4) of data for similar transcription errors. You also commit to sending “ (b)(4) samples of impacted drug product including (b)(4) ” to a contract testing laboratory.
Your response is inadequate because it fails to address the severity of the observed data integrity failures. Your proposed corrective actions address the data integrity breaches as isolated procedural gaps rather than as evidence of a systemic breakdown in QU oversight and a deficient quality culture. Your response does not address the fundamental failure of your QU to ensure the integrity and completeness of all data related to your drug manufacturing operations, nor does it include an adequate assessment of the potential impact on the quality of drug products already distributed to the U.S. market. Furthermore, your response lacks a sufficient comprehensive evaluation of your QU’s capabilities to fulfill all required quality-related functions.
Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. Thereafter, ongoing vigilant oversight of process performance and drug product quality is necessary to ensure you maintain a stable manufacturing operation throughout the drug product lifecycle. 본 경고 서한은 완제품 의약품에 대한 현행 우수제조관리기준(현행 우수제조관리기준(CGMP)) 법규 위반의 중대한 사항들을 요약한 것입니다. 미국 연방법규(Code of Federal Regulations) Title 21 법규 편(parts) 210 및 211 를(을) 참조하십시오 (21 CFR parts 210 및 211).

귀사의 제조, 가공, 충전 또는 보관을 위한 방법, 시설 또는 관리체계가 CGMP에 부합하지 않기 때문에, 귀사의 의약품은 연방법인 식품, 의약품 및 화장품법(Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, FD&C Act) 501(a)(2)(B)의 의미상 오염(adulterated)에 해당하며, 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B)입니다.

FDA 실사 동안, 당사 조사관은 다음을 포함하되 이에 국한되지 않는 특정 위반 사항을 관찰했습니다.

sections.title: 1. 귀사는 모든 성분, 의약품 용기, 마개, 공정 중 자재, 포장 자재, 라벨링 및 의약품을 승인하거나 거부할 책임과 권한을 가지며, 생산 기록을 검토하여 오류가 발생하지 않았음을 또는 오류가 발생했다면 그 오류가 완전히 조사되었음을 보증할 책임과 권한을 갖는 적절한 품질부서(QU)를 수립하지 못했습니다 (21 CFR 211.22(a)).
items: 귀사는 (b)(4) 및 (b)(4) 를 포함한 일반의약품(OTC)을 제조합니다. 귀사의 품질부서(QU)는 생산 기록의 무결성을 보장하는 것을 포함하여 의약품 제조 운영에 대한 권한과 책임을 행사하지 못했습니다.

실사 중에 조사관은 귀 경영진이 전적으로 (b)(4) 제조에 전담된 것이라고 진술한 Unit (b)(4) , Line (b)(4) 의 장비 사용 로그북을 요청했습니다. 귀사는 이 기록을 제공하는 것을 수일간 지연시켰습니다. 귀사가 마침내 로그북을 제시했을 때 해당 로그북은 새로 작성된 것처럼 보였습니다. 이후 조사관은 원본 로그북을 문서 보관실에서 발견했습니다. 두 로그북을 비교한 결과, 조사관에게 제공된 버전은 위조된 것으로 드러났습니다. 위조된 로그북에는 오직 (b)(4) 에 대한 항목만 기재되어 있었고, 원본 로그북에 문서화된 여러 미국 시장에 유통된 OTC 의약품들—그 중에는 (b)(4) 도 포함됩니다—에 대한 항목을 고의적으로 누락했습니다.

또한 조사관은 귀사의 분석 데이터 북에 있는 원자료와 배치 제조 기록 또는 시험성적서에 보고된 최종 값 사이에 다수의 불일치를 확인했습니다. (b)(4) 및 (b)(4) 의 여러 배치에서 강열잔분, 용융 범위, pH 및 점도와 같은 품질 속성에 대해 보고된 값이 원자료와 일치하지 않았습니다. 이러한 부정확성은 규격 일탈(OOS) 결과와 관련되지는 않았지만, 귀사의 품질부서(QU)는 데이터의 일관성과 정확성을 확보하지 않은 채 해당 기록들에 서명했습니다.

귀사의 회신에서 귀사는 이들 결함을 인정하면서 위조된 로그북은 “부적절한 문서 통제, 불충분한 감독, 견고한 관리 체계의 부재” 때문이라고 기술했습니다. 귀사는 다른 데이터 부정확성들을 전사 관행과 품질부서(QU) 내의 적절한 검토에 필요한 자원의 부족 탓으로 돌렸습니다. 귀사는 데이터 무결성에 대해 직원 교육을 실시했으며 절차를 개정하고 유사한 전사 오류에 대해서는 데이터의 (b)(4) 만 검토하겠다고 약속했습니다. 또한 귀사는 “(b)(4) 표본의 영향을 받은 의약품을 포함한 (b)(4)” 를 수탁 시험기관으로 보낼 것을 약속했습니다.

귀사의 회신은 관찰된 데이터 무결성 실패의 심각성을 다루지 않으므로 부적절합니다. 귀사가 제시한 시정조치는 데이터 무결성 위반을 단지 절차적 허점으로만 다루고 있으며, 이는 품질부서(QU) 감독의 체계적 붕괴 및 결함 있는 품질 문화의 증거로 보는 데 실패하고 있습니다. 귀사의 회신은 의약품 제조 운영과 관련된 모든 데이터의 무결성과 완전성을 보장하지 못한 품질부서(QU)의 근본적 실패를 다루지 않으며, 미국 시장에 이미 유통된 의약품의 품질에 미칠 수 있는 잠재적 영향에 대한 적절한 평가를 포함하지 않습니다. 또한 귀사의 회신에는 품질부서(QU)가 모든 필수 품질 관련 기능을 수행할 수 있는 역량에 대한 충분하고 포괄적인 평가가 결여되어 있습니다.

귀사의 품질 시스템은 불충분합니다. 품질 시스템을 구현하고 위험 관리 접근법을 통해 CGMP 규정 요구사항을 충족하는 데 도움이 되는 FDA의 지침서 "Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical CGMP Regulations"(의약품 CGMP 규정에 대한 품질 시스템 접근법)를 참조하시기 바랍니다 21 CFR, parts 210 and 211 에 대한 자세한 내용은 https://www.fda.gov/media/71023/download.
본 서신에 회신하실 때 다음을 제출하십시오:

제조 및 실험실 운영 전반에 사용되는 문서 시스템에 대한 포괄적인 평가를 제출하여 문서 작성 관행이 불충분한 지점을 확인하십시오. 작성자를 식별할 수 있는 기록, 읽기 가능한 기록, 완전한 기록, 원본 기록, 정확한 기록, 작업 시점에 작성된 기록을 운영 전반에 걸쳐 보유하도록 귀사의 문서 관행을 포괄적으로 시정하는 상세한 시정조치 및 예방조치(CAPA) 계획을 포함하십시오.

품질부서(QU)가 효과적으로 기능할 수 있도록 권한과 자원을 부여받았는지 확인하기 위한 포괄적인 평가 및 개선 계획을 제출하십시오. 평가는 다음을 포함하되 이에 국한되지 않아야 합니다: o 귀사가 사용하는 절차들이 견고하고 적절한지 여부에 대한 결정 o 적절한 관행 준수를 평가하기 위해 운영 전반에서 품질부서(QU)의 감독을 위한 조항 o 품질부서(QU)의 최종 판정 결정 전에 각 배치 및 관련 정보를 완전하고 최종적으로 검토하는 절차 o 모든 제품의 동일성, 강도, 품질 및 순도를 보장하기 위한 조사 승인과 기타 모든 품질부서(QU) 업무의 감독 및 승인

sections.title: 2. 귀사는 수립된 규격 및 기준에 대한 준수를 보장하는 데 필요한 모든 시험에서 도출된 완전한 데이터를 포함하도록 실험실 기록을 작성하지 않았습니다 (21 CFR 211.194(a)).
items: 귀사의 실험실 기록은 수행된 분석을 지원하기 위한 완전한 데이터를 포함하지 않았습니다. 예를 들어 귀사의 분석 노트북은 완제품에 대한 약 (b)(4) 개의 미생물학 접시와 (b)(4) 개의 (b)(4) 시료 시험을 위한 배지 접시가 배양된 것으로 문서화되어 있으나, 해당 접시들은 배양기에서 물리적으로 누락되어 있거나 그 행방 또는 폐기에 대한 문서화된 설명이 없었습니다. 또한 실사 중 귀사는 약 (b)(4) 배치의 미국 판매 의약품에 대해 보고된 시험성적서 결과를 뒷받침할 시험 절차, 분석 워크북 또는 시험 데이터 시트를 제시하지 못했습니다. 귀사는 또한 특정 배치 방출 시험에 사용된 다수의 기기 사용을 반영하도록 장비 로그북에 필요한 기재를 하지 못했습니다.
귀사의 회신에서, 귀사는 미생물학자가 훈련 부족으로 인해 누락된 미생물 검사용 플레이트를 실수로 폐기했다고 밝혔습니다. 귀사는 해당 미생물학자를 재교육했고, 누락된 완제품 플레이트를 재분석했으며, 샘플 추적성을 개선하기 위해 새로운 통제된 로그북을 도입했다고 진술하였습니다.

지원 분석 기록 없이 출고된 배치들에 관해, 귀사는 그 배치들 중 여러 건의 샘플을 소급 시험을 위하여 수탁 검사기관으로 보낼 것을 약속하고, 향후 데이터 기록을 위해 정식 시험 데이터 시트를 도입할 것이라고 약속하였습니다. 아울러, 귀사는 기기 사용 기록을 문서화하지 못한 담당자들을 재교육했으며 새로운 데이터 시트가 도입되면 별도의 장비 사용 로그북의 사용을 중단할 것이라고 밝혔습니다.

귀사의 회신은 실험실 시스템의 중대한 결함을 적절히 다루지 않았기 때문에 부적절합니다. 귀사의 회신은 품질부서(QU)를 포함하되 이에 국한되지 않는 데이터 무결성 감독을 개선하는 것을 포함하여 데이터 무결성에 대한 귀사의 감독을 해결하지 못합니다. 귀사의 회신은 포괄적인 소급적 위험 평가나 유효기간 내에서 잠재적으로 영향받을 수 있는 모든 의약품의 완전한 시험을 제공하지 못하며 소비자에 대한 위험을 적절히 평가하고 완화하지 못합니다.
데이터를 기록하지 않거나 시험 결과의 완전하고 정확한 기록을 유지하지 못할 경우 데이터의 신뢰성은 근본적으로 훼손됩니다. 더 나아가, 신뢰할 수 있는 데이터의 부재는 귀사의 품질부서(QU)가 적용 가능한 기준 준수를 보장하는 기능을 수행하는 능력을 약화시킵니다.

귀사의 품질 시스템은 귀사가 제조하는 의약품의 안전성, 유효성 및 품질을 뒷받침할 데이터의 정확성과 무결성을 적절히 보장하지 못합니다. GMP에 따른 데이터 무결성 관행 수립 및 준수에 관한 안내는 FDA의 지침서 Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Questions and Answers에서 확인하시기 바랍니다: https://www.fda.gov/media/119267/download.
귀사의 시정조치를 지원하기 위해 독립적인 제3자 적격 컨설턴트를 선임할 것을 강력히 권고합니다. 본 서한에 대한 회신으로, 다음을 제출하십시오:

기록 및 보고의 부정확성 범위에 대한 포괄적 조사. 귀사의 조사는 다음을 포함해야 합니다: o 상세한 조사 계획서 및 방법론; 평가에 포함될 모든 시험실, 제조 공정 및 시스템의 요약; 제외를 제안하는 귀사 운영의 어느 부분에 대한 근거 설명. o 데이터 부정확성의 성격, 범위 및 근본원인을 규명하기 위한 현재 및 전직 직원들과의 면담. 이러한 면담은 자격을 갖춘 제3자가 수행할 것을 권고합니다. o 귀사 시설에서의 데이터 무결성 결함의 정도에 대한 평가. 누락, 변경, 삭제, 기록 파기, 작업 시점에 작성되지 않은 기록(비동시 기록 작성), 기타 결함을 식별하십시오. 귀사 시설 운영의 어느 부분에서 데이터 무결성 위반이 발견되었는지 모두 기술하십시오. o 모든 데이터 무결성 결함의 성격에 대한 포괄적인 소급 평가. 잠재적 위반이 확인된 분야에 특화된 전문지식을 보유한 자격 있는 제3자가 모든 데이터 무결성 위반을 평가할 것을 권고합니다.
관찰된 실패가 귀사의 의약품 품질에 미칠 잠재적 영향에 대한 최신 위험 평가. 귀사의 평가는 데이터 무결성 위반으로 영향을 받은 의약품의 유통으로 인한 환자 위험에 대한 분석과 계속되는 운영으로 인해 제기되는 위험 분석을 포함해야 합니다.

귀사의 경영 전략으로서 전사적 시정조치 및 예방조치(CAPA) 계획의 세부사항을 포함한 관리 전략. 귀사의 전략에는 다음이 포함되어야 합니다: o 귀사가 생성하는 모든 데이터(분석 데이터, 제조 기록 및 FDA에 제출되는 모든 데이터 포함)의 신뢰성 및 완전성을 보장하기 위한 방법을 설명하는 상세한 시정조치 계획. o 데이터 무결성 위반의 근본원인에 대한 포괄적 기술과, 현재의 조치 계획의 범위 및 깊이가 조사 결과 및 위험 평가 결과와 상응함을 입증하는 증거. 데이터 무결성 위반에 책임이 있는 개인이 귀사에서 CGMP 관련 또는 의약품 신청 데이터에 영향을 미칠 수 있는지 여부를 명시하십시오. o 환자를 보호하고 귀사 의약품의 품질을 보장하기 위해 취했거나 취할 중간 조치들(예: 고객 통지, 제품 회수, 추가 시험 수행, 안정성 보장을 위한 제조번호의 안정성 프로그램 추가, 의약품 신청 관련 조치 및 강화된 불만 모니터링) 설명. o 절차, 공정, 방법, 통제, 시스템, 경영 감독 및 인적 자원(예: 교육, 인력 개선)을 포함한 시정 조치 및 개선을 통해 귀사 데이터의 무결성을 보장하기 위한 장기적 조치 및 개선 노력 설명. o 귀사의 데이터 무결성 개선 절차를 실행한 후 CAPA 효과성을 평가하는 데 도움을 주기 위해 최소 두 해 동안 자격 있는 컨설턴트가 광범위한 연례 감사를 수행하도록 하겠다는 약속. o 직원이 데이터 무결성 문제를 익명으로 제보할 수 있도록 접수할 수 있는 완전한 권한을 부여받고, 독립 품질보증 기능과 필요시 외부 전문 인력의 전문성을 통해 잠재적 위반을 신속히 조사할 권한을 가진 최고무결성책임자(Chief Integrity Officer)를 채용할 것인지 여부를 FDA에 통지할 것. o 위에 열거된 활동 중 이미 진행 중이거나 완료된 활동에 대한 상태 보고.

sections.title: 3. 귀사는 장비의 세척 및 유지보수에 대한 적절한 서면 절차를 수립하고 준수하지 않았습니다 (21 CFR 211.67(b)).
items: 귀사는 OTC 의약품 제조에 사용되는 공용(비전용) 장비에서 잠재적 오염물질을 제거하고 제품 간 오염(제품 이행, carry over)을 방지하기에 세척 관행이 적절하다는 것을 입증하지 못했습니다.

예를 들어, 비전용 Unit (b)(4) Line (b)(4)에 대한 귀사의 세척 검증 프로그램은 적절한 세척 여부를 판단하기 위해 전적으로 (b)(4)의 육안 검사에 의존했습니다. 귀사의 세척 검증 프로그램에는 과학적으로 결정된 최대 허용 이행 한계, 정량적 잔류물 시험, 또는 세척이 어려운 부위에 대한 직접 표면 채취 검사가 결여되어 있습니다. 또한 귀사는 최소 (b)(4)개의 서로 다른 OTC 의약품을 제조하는 데 사용하는 Unit (b)(4) Line (b)(4)에 대해 아무런 세척 검증도 수행하지 않았습니다.

귀사의 회신에서 귀사는 세정(클리닝) 유효성 검증 프로그램의 결함을 인정하였습니다. 귀사는 검증된 분석법을 개발하고, 이행 잔류 허용한계를 설정하며, 직접 표면 스왑(면봉) 샘플링을 시행하고, 세정 공정을 재검증하는 방식으로 귀사의 세정 유효성 검증 프로그램을 강화하겠다고 약속했습니다. 귀사는 (b)(4) 라인이 현재 (b)(4) 의약품 전용으로 사용되고 있으며, 제한적인 소급적 품질 검토(retrospective quality review)를 수행하여 잠재적 교차오염을 확인하기 위해 오직 (b)(4) 샘플만 시험하고 있다고 진술했습니다.

귀사의 회신은 불충분합니다. 귀사는 시정조치 기간 동안 교차오염 위험을 완화하기 위해 어떤 임시 통제를 시행할 것인지에 관해 언급하지 않았습니다. 또한 (b)(4) 라인에서 제조된 (b)(4) 배치에서 단지 (b)(4) 샘플만 검사하는 것은 교차오염 가능성을 평가하기에 통계적으로 불충분합니다. 아울러 귀사의 회신에는 전용 장비가 아닌 장비에 대해 비검증된 세정 공정을 사용함으로 인해 발생했을 수 있는 잠재적 교차오염을 조사하기 위한, 유통을 위해 출시되어 있고 유효기간 내인 모든 의약품에 대한 소급 검토(retrospective review)가 포함되어 있지 않습니다.
전용이 아닌 제조장비 표면에서 활성성분 및 의약품 잔류물이 적절히 제거되지 않으면 이후에 해당 장비에서 제조되는 의약품이 오염될 수 있습니다.
이 서한에 회신하실 때 다음을 제출하십시오:

시설 및 장비에 대한 일상적이고 면밀한 운영 관리 감시를 시행하기 위한 귀사의 시정조치/예방조치(CAPA) 계획. 이 계획에는 자격을 갖춘 독립 컨설턴트의 감시를 포함시키고, 그 안에서 장비·시설 성능 문제의 신속한 감지, 수리의 효과적인 실행, 적절한 예방정비 일정의 준수, 장비·시설 인프라의 시기적절한 기술적 업그레이드, 그리고 지속적인 경영 검토를 위한 개선된 시스템 등을 보장해야 합니다. 귀사의 계획은 회사 네트워크 전반에 걸쳐 적절한 조치가 취해지도록 보장해야 합니다.

교차오염 위해요인의 범위를 평가하기 위한 귀사의 세정 유효성에 대한 포괄적이고 독립적인 소급적 평가(retrospective assessment). 여기에는 잔류물의 정체, 부적절하게 세정되었을 수 있는 다른 제조장비, 그리고 교차오염된 의약품이 유통을 위해 출시되었을 가능성에 대한 평가를 포함하십시오. 이 평가는 세정 절차 및 관행의 어떠한 부적절성도 식별해야 하며, 두 가지 이상의 의약품을 제조하는 데 사용되는 각 제조장비를 모두 포괄해야 합니다.

귀사의 세정 유효성 검증 프로그램에 대한 적절한 개선책, 특히 귀사의 의약품 제조 작업에서 최악의 경우(최악 사례)로 규명된 조건들을 포함하도록 강조하십시오. 여기에는 다음의 최악 사례를 식별하고 평가하는 것을 포함하되 이에 국한되지 않습니다: o 독성이 더 높은 의약품 o 약효(효능)가 더 높은 의약품 o 세정용매에서 용해도가 낮은 의약품 o 세척이 어렵게 하는 특성을 가진 의약품 o 세척이 가장 어려운 영역에 대한 스왑(면봉) 채취 위치 o 세정 전 최대 보관 시간(최대 보관기간)
또한, 신규 제조장비 또는 신규 의약품을 도입하기 전에 귀사의 변경관리(change management) 시스템에서 취해야 할 조치 단계를 설명하십시오.
의약품, 공정 및 장비에 대한 세정 절차의 검증 및 확인을 위한 적절한 프로그램이 마련되었음을 보장하는 업데이트된 표준작업지침서(SOP) 요약을 제출하십시오.

sections.title: 4. 귀사는 제조하는 의약품이 주장하거나 표시한 정체성, 함량, 품질 및 순도를 보유하고 있음을 보증하도록 설계된 생산 및 공정 관리에 관한 충분한 서면 절차를 수립하지 못하였으며, 귀사의 품질관리부서(quality control unit)는 해당 절차(및 변경사항 포함)를 검토·승인하지 않았습니다(21 CFR 211.100(a)).
items: 귀사는 귀사의 일반의약품(OTC) 제조공정에 대한 공정 검증(process validation)을 수행하지 못했습니다. 실사 중에 귀사는 (b)(4) 라인의 제조에서 귀사가 제조하는 (b)(4) 의약품 중 (b)(4) 에 대해 공정 검증을 수행하지 않았다고 진술했습니다. 또한 귀사는 (b)(4) 라인의 제조에서 귀사가 제조하는 (b)(4) 의약품 중 (b)(4) 에 대해 공정 검증을 수행하지 않았다고 진술했습니다.
귀사의 회신에서 귀사는 대부분의 의약품에 대한 공정 검증이 부족함을 인정하고 캠페인 기반 접근법을 사용하여 공정 검증 계획 및 프로토콜을 준비하겠다고 약속했습니다.

귀사의 회신은 불충분합니다. 각 의약품별 공정 검증 활동을 완료하기 위한 일정 또는 기한을 제시하지 않았기 때문입니다. 또한 검증 활동이 완료되기 전에 제조·유통되는 어떠한 의약품에 대해서도 허용 가능한 품질의 의약품을 생산하고 있음을 보장하기 위한 강화된 완제품 검사와 같은 중간 계획이 회신에 포함되어 있지 않습니다. 또한 유효기간 내에 있고 계속 제조 중인 미국 유통 의약품에 대한 의약품 영향 평가를 제공하지 않았습니다.

공정 검증은 설계의 타당성과 공정 수명 주기 전반에 걸친 관리 상태를 평가합니다. 제조 공정의 각 중요한 단계는 적절하게 설계되어야 하며 원료 투입물, 공정 중 재료 및 완제품의 품질을 보증해야 합니다. 공정 적격성 시험(프로세스 퀄리피케이션)에는 배치 내 변동을 특성화하고 초기 관리 상태가 확립되었는지 판단하기 위해 각 중요한 공정 단계 전반에 걸친 집중적인 모니터링 및 시험이 포함됩니다.

상업적 유통 이전에 공정 적격성 시험의 성공이 필요합니다. 그 이후로는 공정 성능과 완제품 품질에 대한 지속적이고 철저한 감독이 필요하여 의약품 수명 주기 동안 안정적인 제조 운영을 유지해야 합니다. 일반적인 원칙과 접근법으로 FDA가 공정 검증의 적절한 요소로 간주하는 사항은 FDA의 산업체용 가이드라인, Process Validation: General Principles and Practices(공정 검증: 일반 원칙 및 실제)를 참조하십시오 https://www.fda.gov/media/71021/download.
이 서한에 대한 회신으로 다음을 제출하십시오:
제품 수명 주기 전반에 걸쳐 관리 상태를 보장하기 위한 귀사의 검증 프로그램에 대한 상세 요약과 관련 절차. 공정 성능 적격성(program for process performance qualification) 및 배치 내·배치 간 변동을 지속적으로 모니터링하여 계속된 관리 상태를 보장하기 위한 귀사의 프로그램을 설명하십시오.
시장에 유통 중인 각 의약품에 대해 공정 성능 적격성 수행 일정표를 제출하십시오.
공정 성능 프로토콜 및 장비와 시설의 적격성(qualification)을 위한 서면 절차를 제출하십시오.
각 제조 공정을 설계, 검증, 유지, 통제 및 모니터링하기 위한 상세 프로그램을 제출하십시오. 이 프로그램에는 계속된 관리 상태를 보장하기 위한 배치 내 및 배치 간 변동에 대한 철저한 모니터링이 포함되어야 합니다. 또한 장비 및 시설의 적격성 프로그램을 포함하십시오.

sections.title: 의약품 리콜
items: May 13, 2026 에 FDA는 귀사와 전화 회의를 갖고 미국 시장에서 현재 유통 중인 모든 (b)(4) 배치의 회수를 검토할 것을 권고했습니다.
June 2, 2026 에 귀사는 시설의 전반적 품질 실패로 인해 모든 (b)(4) 및 (b)(4)의 자발적 회수를 발표했습니다. 현재까지 귀사는 귀사의 (b)(4) 의약품을 회수하지 않았습니다.

sections.title: CGMP 컨설턴트 권고
items: 미국 시장을 대상으로 의약품 제조를 재개하려는 경우, 귀사는 운영을 평가하고 우수 제조관리기준(CGMP) 요구사항을 충족하도록 돕기 위해 자격을 갖춘 컨설턴트를 고용해야 합니다. 해당 자격 있는 컨설턴트는 또한 CGMP 준수 여부를 확인하기 위해 귀사의 전 운영에 대해 포괄적인 여섯 개 시스템 감사를 수행하고, 귀사가 이행한 시정조치 및 예방조치의 완료 여부와 효과성을 평가해야 합니다. 그런 후에야 귀사는 FDA와 귀사의 준법 상태 해결을 추진할 수 있습니다.
컨설턴트의 고용은 귀사가 CGMP를 준수할 의무를 면제하지 않습니다. 귀사의 최고 경영진은 모든 결함과 체계적 결함을 해결하여 지속적인 CGMP 준수를 보장할 책임이 있습니다.

sections.title: 결론
items: 이 서한에서 지적한 위반사항은 귀 시설에 존재하는 모든 위반사항을 포괄적으로 열거한 것이 아닙니다. 귀사는 모든 위반의 원인을 조사하고 규명하며, 그 재발 또는 다른 위반의 발생을 방지할 책임이 있습니다.
FDA는 귀사에서 미국으로 수입 제출된 모든 의약품 및 의약품 제품을 66-40 수입 경보(Import Alert)에 등재했으며, 등재일은 June 5, 2026 입니다.
위반사항을 신속히 시정하십시오. 귀사가 제조업체로 기재된 신규 신청서나 보완 신청서에 대한 승인 보류는 모든 위반이 완전히 시정되고 저희가 귀사의 CGMP 준수를 확인할 때까지 계속될 수 있습니다. 저희는 귀사가 모든 위반에 대한 시정조치를 완료했는지 확인하기 위해 재실사를 할 수 있습니다.

어떠한 위반도 시정하지 않을 경우, Dabur India Limited, at Survey No. 225/4/1, Village: Saily, Silvassa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu에서 제조된 물품의 미국 입국을 801(a)(3) 조항에 따라 계속 거부할 수 있습니다(미국 연방 식품, 의약품, 화장품법(FD&C Act)). 21 U.S.C. 381(a)(3). 이 권한에 따라 변질(adulterated)으로 보이는 물품은 제조 방법과 관리가 CGMP에 부합하지 않는 것으로 보여 압수되거나 입국이 거부될 수 있으며, 이는 FD&C 법의 501(a)(2)(B) 조항의 의미 내에서 CGMP에 부합하지 않는 것으로 보인다는 것을 의미합니다. 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B).

이 서한은 저희의 조사 결과를 통지하고 위의 결함을 시정할 기회를 제공합니다. 이 서한을 받은 후, 서면으로 본 실무부서에 15 근무일 이내에 회신하십시오. 어떤 위반을 시정하기 위해 귀사가 수행한 조치와 그 재발 방지 조치를 명시하십시오. 이 서한에 대한 회신으로 귀사는 저희가 귀사의 활동과 관행을 계속 평가하는 동안 고려할 추가 정보를 제출할 수 있습니다. 만약 15 근무일 이내에 시정조치를 완료할 수 없다면, 지연 사유와 완료 일정(스케줄)을 명시하십시오.
전자 회신은 CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov로 보내십시오. 귀사의 회신에 FEI 3001413302 및 수신처(ATTN): Rokhsana Safaai-Jazi를 식별자로 표기하십시오.
Sincerely, /S/

Francis Godwin
제조 품질 실장(Director), 준수국(Office of Compliance), 의약품 평가 및 연구 센터(Center for Drug Evaluation and Research)

Warning Letter 320-26-105
July 24, 2026
Dear Mr. Malhotra:
The United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) inspected your drug manufacturing facility, Dabur India Limited, FEI 3001413302, at Survey No. 225/4/1, Village: Saily, Silvassa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, from January 12 to 16, 2026.
This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), parts 210 and 211 (21 CFR parts 210 and 211).
Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding do not conform to CGMP, your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B).
We reviewed your February 4, 2026 response to our Form FDA 483 in detail.
During our inspection, our investigator observed specific violations including, but not limited to, the following.

sources.label: Dabur India Limited · 1. Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality control unit with the responsibility and authority to approve or reject all components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, packaging materials, labeling, and drug products and the authority to review production records to assure that no errors have occurred or, if errors have occurred, that they have been fully investigated (21 CFR 211.22(a)).
sources.excerpt:
1. Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality control unit with the responsibility and authority to approve or reject all components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, packaging materials, labeling, and drug products and the authority to review production records to assure that no errors have occurred or, if errors have occurred, that they have been fully investigated (21 CFR 211.22(a)).
Your firm manufactures over-the-counter drug products including (b)(4) and (b)(4) . Your quality unit (QU) failed to exercise its authority and responsibilities over your drug manufacturing operations, including ensuring the integrity of your production records.
During the inspection, our investigator requested the equipment usage logbook for Unit (b)(4) , Line (b)(4) , which your management stated was dedicated exclusively to (b)(4) manufacturing. Your firm delayed providing this record for several days. When your firm finally produced the logbook, it appeared to have been newly created. Subsequently, our investigator discovered the original logbook in the document room. A comparison of the two logbooks revealed that the version provided to our investigator was falsified. The fraudulent logbook listed entries only for (b)(4) . It deliberately omitted multiple U.S. marketed OTC drug products that were documented in the original logbook, including (b)(4) .
Furthermore, our investigator identified multiple discrepancies between the source data in your analytical data books and the final values reported in your batch manufacturing records or certificates of analysis. For multiple batches of (b)(4) and (b)(4) , the reported values for quality attributes such as residue on ignition, melting range, pH, and viscosity did not match the original data. While these inaccuracies did not involve out-of-specification results, your QU signed off on these records without ensuring the consistency and accuracy of the data.
In your response, you acknowledge these deficiencies, attributing the falsified logbook to “inadequate documentation controls, insufficient oversight, and lack of robust governance.” You attributed other data inaccuracies to your transcription practices and inadequate resources within your QU for proper review. You state that you trained personnel on data integrity and committed to revising procedures and reviewing only the (b)(4) of data for similar transcription errors. You also commit to sending “ (b)(4) samples of impacted drug product including (b)(4) ” to a contract testing laboratory.
Your response is inadequate because it fails to address the severity of the observed data integrity failures. Your proposed corrective actions address the data integrity breaches as isolated procedural gaps rather than as evidence of a systemic breakdown in QU oversight and a deficient quality culture. Your response does not address the fundamental failure of your QU to ensure the integrity and completeness of all data related to your drug manufacturing operations, nor does it include an adequate assessment of the potential impact on the quality of drug products already distributed to the U.S. market. Furthermore, your response lacks a sufficient comprehensive evaluation of your QU’s capabilities to fulfill all required quality-related functions.
Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. See FDA’s guidance document Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical CGMP Regulations for help implementing quality systems and risk management approaches to meet the requirements of CGMP regulations 21 CFR, parts 210 and 211 at https://www.fda.gov/media/71023/download.
In response to this letter, provide:
A comprehensive assessment of documentation systems used throughout your manufacturing and laboratory operations to determine where documentation practices are insufficient. Include a detailed corrective action and preventive action (CAPA) plan that comprehensively remediates your firm’s documentation practices to ensure you retain attributable, legible, complete, original, accurate, contemporaneous records throughout your operation.
A comprehensive assessment and remediation plan to ensure your QU is given the authority and resources to effectively function. The assessment should also include, but not be limited to: o A determination of whether procedures used by your firm are robust and appropriate o Provisions for QU oversight throughout your operations to evaluate adherence to appropriate practices o A complete and final review of each batch and its related information before the QU disposition decision o Oversight and approval of investigations and discharging of all other QU duties to ensure identity, strength, quality, and purity of all products.

sources.label: Dabur India Limited · 2. Your firm failed to ensure that laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests necessary to ensure compliance with established specifications and standards (21 CFR 211.194(a)).
sources.excerpt:
2. Your firm failed to ensure that laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests necessary to ensure compliance with established specifications and standards (21 CFR 211.194(a)).
Your laboratory records did not include complete data to support the analyses performed. For example, your analytical notebooks documented approximately (b)(4) microbiology plates for finished drug products and approximately (b)(4) media plates for testing (b)(4) samples as incubated, but the plates were physically absent from incubators with no documented explanation about their whereabouts or disposal. In addition, during the inspection you could not produce the test procedures, analytical workbooks, or test data sheets to support the reported certificate of analysis results for approximately (b)(4) batches of U.S. marketed drug products. You also failed to make the required entries in your equipment logbooks to reflect the use of multiple instruments for the specific batch release tests performed.
In your response, you indicate that a microbiologist inadvertently discarded the missing microbiological plates due to lack of training. You state that you retrained the microbiologist, re-analyzed the missing finished drug product plates, and introduced a new controlled logbook to improve sample traceability.
Regarding the batches released without supporting analytical records, you commit to sending samples for several of the batches to a contract laboratory for retrospective testing and to implementing formal test data sheets for future data recording. Further, you state that you have retrained the personnel responsible for failing to document instrument usage and that you will discontinue the use of separate equipment usage logbooks once the new data sheets are implemented.
Your response is inadequate because it does not adequately address major deficiencies in your laboratory system. Your response does not address your oversight of data integrity including, but not limited to, improving your quality assurance function. Your response does not provide a comprehensive retrospective risk assessment or complete testing of all potentially impacted drug products within expiry and fails to adequately assess and mitigate the risk to consumers.
Reliability of data is fundamentally compromised when there is a failure to record data or to maintain complete and accurate records of test results. Furthermore, the lack of reliable data compromises the ability of your QU to exercise its function of ensuring compliance to applicable standards.
Your quality system does not adequately ensure the accuracy and integrity of data to support the safety, effectiveness, and quality of the drugs you manufacture. See FDA’s guidance document Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP: Questions and Answers for guidance on establishing and following CGMP compliant data integrity practices at https://www.fda.gov/media/119267/download.
We strongly recommend that you retain an independent third-party qualified consultant to assist in your remediation. In response to this letter, provide:
A comprehensive investigation into the extent of the inaccuracies in data records and reporting. Your investigation should include: o A detailed investigation protocol and methodology; a summary of all laboratories, manufacturing operations, and systems to be covered by the assessment; and a justification for any part of your operation that you propose to exclude. o Interviews of current and former employees to identify the nature, scope, and root cause of data inaccuracies. We recommend that these interviews be conducted by a qualified third party. o An assessment of the extent of data integrity deficiencies at your facility. Identify omissions, alterations, deletions, record destruction, non-contemporaneous record completion, and other deficiencies. Describe all parts of your facility’s operations in which you discovered data integrity lapses. o A comprehensive retrospective evaluation of the nature of all data integrity deficiencies. We recommend that a qualified third party with specific expertise in the area where potential breaches were identified should evaluate all data integrity lapses.
A current risk assessment of the potential effects of the observed failures on the quality of your drugs. Your assessment should include analyses of the risks to patients caused by the release of drugs affected by a lapse of data integrity and analyses of the risks posed by ongoing operations.
A management strategy for your firm that includes the details of your global corrective action and preventive action plan. Your strategy should include: o A detailed corrective action plan that describes how you intend to ensure the reliability and completeness of all the data you generate including analytical data, manufacturing records, and all data submitted to FDA. o A comprehensive description of the root causes of your data integrity lapses including evidence that the scope and depth of the current action plan is commensurate with the findings of the investigation and risk assessment. Indicate whether individuals responsible for data integrity lapses remain able to influence CGMP-related or drug application data at your firm. o Interim measures describing the actions you have taken or will take to protect patients and to ensure the quality of your drugs, such as notifying your customers, recalling product, conducting additional testing, adding lots to your stability programs to assure stability, drug application actions, and enhanced complaint monitoring. o Long-term measures describing any remediation efforts and enhancements to procedures, processes, methods, controls, systems, management oversight, and human resources (e.g., training, staffing improvements) designed to ensure the integrity of your company’s data. o A commitment to have a qualified consultant conduct extensive annual audits, for at least two years, to assist in evaluating CAPA effectiveness after you have executed your data integrity remediation protocol. o Inform FDA if you will be hiring a Chief Integrity Officer who is fully empowered to receive anonymous complaints from employees reporting data integrity concerns and with the authority to ensure any potential breach is promptly investigated (by independent quality assurance function, along with expertise from outside entities whenever needed). o A status report for any of the above activities already underway or completed.

sources.label: Dabur India Limited · 3. Your firm failed to establish and follow adequate written procedures for cleaning and maintenance of equipment (21 CFR 211.67(b)).
sources.excerpt:
3. Your firm failed to establish and follow adequate written procedures for cleaning and maintenance of equipment (21 CFR 211.67(b)).
You failed to demonstrate that your cleaning practices are adequate to remove potential contaminants and to prevent drug product carry over in shared equipment used to manufacture your OTC drug products.
For example, your cleaning validation program for the non-dedicated Unit (b)(4) Line (b)(4) relied exclusively on the visual inspection of (b)(4) to determine adequate cleaning. Your cleaning validation program lacked scientifically determined maximum allowable carryover limits, quantitative residue testing, or direct surface sampling of difficult-to-clean areas. In addition, you did not perform any cleaning validation for Unit (b)(4) Line (b)(4) despite using it to manufacture at least (b)(4) different OTC drug products.
In your response, you acknowledge the deficiencies in your cleaning validation program. You commit to enhancing your cleaning validation program by developing validated analytical methods, establishing carryover limits, implementing direct surface swab sampling, and revalidating the cleaning process. You stated that Line (b)(4) is now dedicated to a (b)(4) drug product, and you are conducting a limited retrospective quality review by testing only (b)(4) samples for potential cross-contamination.
Your response is inadequate because it does not address the interim controls you will implement to mitigate the risk of cross-contamination during your remediation period. Additionally, testing only (b)(4) samples from the (b)(4) batches manufactured on Line (b)(4) is statistically insufficient to assess the potential for cross-contamination. Further, your response also does not include a retrospective review of all drug products released to the U.S. market and within expiry for potential cross-contamination resulting from the use of a non-validated cleaning process on non-dedicated equipment.
Inadequate removal of active ingredients and drug product residues from surfaces of non-dedicated manufacturing equipment can lead to contamination of drug products subsequently manufactured on that equipment.
In response to this letter, provide:
Your CAPA plan to implement routine, vigilant operations management oversight of facilities and equipment. This plan should incorporate oversight from a qualified independent consultant and ensure, among other things, prompt detection of equipment/facilities performance issues, effective execution of repairs, adherence to appropriate preventive maintenance schedules, timely technological upgrades to the equipment/facility infrastructure, and improved systems for ongoing management review. Your plan should also ensure that appropriate actions are taken throughout the company network.
A comprehensive, independent retrospective assessment of your cleaning effectiveness to evaluate the scope of cross-contamination hazards. Include the identity of residues, other manufacturing equipment that may have been improperly cleaned, and an assessment whether cross-contaminated drug products may have been released for distribution. The assessment should identify any inadequacies of cleaning procedures and practices, and encompass each piece of manufacturing equipment used to manufacture more than one drug product.
Appropriate improvements to your cleaning validation program, with special emphasis on incorporating conditions identified as worst case in your drug manufacturing operation. This should include but not be limited to identification and evaluation of all worst-case: o drugs with higher toxicities o drugs with higher drug potencies o drugs of lower solubility in their cleaning solvents o drugs with characteristics that make them difficult to clean o swabbing locations for areas that are most difficult to clean o maximum hold times before cleaning
In addition, describe the steps that must be taken in your change management system before introduction of new manufacturing equipment or a new drug product.
A summary of updated SOPs that ensure an appropriate program is in place for verification and validation of cleaning procedures for drug products, processes, and equipment.

Your firm failed to establish adequate written procedures for production and process control designed to assure that the drug products you manufacture have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess, and your firm’s quality control unit did not review and approve those procedures, including any changes (21 CFR 211.100(a)).
sources.excerpt:
4. Your firm failed to establish adequate written procedures for production and process control designed to assure that the drug products you manufacture have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess, and your firm’s quality control unit did not review and approve those procedures, including any changes (21 CFR 211.100(a)).
You failed to validate your manufacturing process for your OTC drug products. During the inspection, you stated that you had not performed process validation for (b)(4) of the (b)(4) drug products you manufacture on Unit (b)(4) lines. You also stated you had not performed process validation for (b)(4) of the (b)(4) drug products you manufacture on Unit (b)(4) lines.
In your response, you acknowledge the lack of process validation for most of your drug products and commit to preparing process validation plans and protocols using a campaign-based approach.
Your response is inadequate because it does not provide a schedule or timeframes for completing process validation activities for each of your drug products. Furthermore, your response lacks an interim plan, such as enhanced finished drug product testing, for any drugs manufactured and distributed before these validation activities are completed to ensure you produce drug products of acceptable quality. You also did not provide drug product impact assessments for U.S. distributed drug products within expiry and ongoing manufacturing.
Process validation evaluates the soundness of design and state of control of a process throughout its lifecycle. Each significant stage of a manufacturing process must be designed appropriately and assure the quality of raw material inputs, in-process materials, and finished drugs. Process qualification studies include intensive monitoring and testing throughout each significant process stage to characterize intra-batch variation and evaluate batches to determine whether an initial state of control has been established.
Successful process qualification studies are necessary before commercial distribution. Thereafter, ongoing vigilant oversight of process performance and drug product quality is necessary to ensure you maintain a stable manufacturing operation throughout the drug product lifecycle. See FDA’s guidance for industry, Process Validation: General Principles and Practices , for general principles and approaches that the FDA considers appropriate elements of process validation at https://www.fda.gov/media/71021/download.
In response to this letter, provide:
A detailed summary of your validation program for ensuring a state of control throughout the product lifecycle, along with associated procedures. Describe your program for process performance qualification and ongoing monitoring of both intra-batch and inter-batch variation to ensure a continuing state of control.
A timeline for performing process performance qualification for each of your marketed drug products.
Process performance protocols, and written procedures for qualification of equipment and facilities.
A detailed program for designing, validating, maintaining, controlling, and monitoring each of your manufacturing processes that includes vigilant monitoring of intra-batch and inter-batch variation to ensure an ongoing state of control. Also, include your program for qualification of your equipment and facility.

Based upon the nature of the violations we identified at your firm, you should engage a consultant qualified to evaluate your operations and to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements if your firm intends to resume manufacturing drugs for the U.S. market. Conclusion
The violations cited in this letter are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of violations that exist at your facility. You are responsible for investigating and determining the causes of any violations and for preventing their recurrence or the occurrence of other violations.
FDA placed all drugs and drug products offered for import into the United States from your firm on Import Alert 66-40 on June 5, 2026.
Correct any violations promptly. FDA may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer until any violations are completely addressed and we confirm your compliance with CGMP. We may re-inspect to verify that you have completed corrective actions to any violations.
Failure to address any violations may also result in the FDA continuing to refuse admission of articles manufactured at Dabur India Limited, at Survey No. 225/4/1, Village: Saily, Silvassa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, into the United States under section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 381(a)(3). This letter notifies you of our findings and provides you an opportunity to address the above deficiencies. After you receive this letter, respond to this office in writing within 15 working days. Specify what you have done to address any violations and to prevent their recurrence. In response to this letter, you may provide additional information for our consideration as we continue to assess your activities and practices. If you cannot complete corrective actions within 15 working days, state your reasons for delay and your schedule for completion.
Send your electronic reply to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov. Identify your response with FEI 3001413302 and ATTN: Rokhsana Safaai-Jazi.
